text.en:
MALACAÑAN PALACE
BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE PHILIPPINES
[ EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 110, December 12, 1947 ]
ORGANIZING THE PHILIPPINE MISSION TO THE UNITED NATIONS AND PROVIDING FOR ITS
DIRECTION AND MAINTENANCE.
By virtue of the powers vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the Republic, and for the purpose of
defining the functions of the Representative of the Philippines at the seat of the United Nations, I, MANUEL
ROXAS, President of the Philippines, hereby order as follows:
1.The representative at the seat of the United Nations as other Representatives of the Philippines to the
General Assembly, the Security Council, the Economic and Social Council, the Trusteeship Council, and the
committees and commissions and sub commissions under them, and to all other organs and agencies of the
United Nations to which the Philippines has been or may hereafter be elected, or of which it has become or
may hereafter become a member, with the exception of those representatives to such international agencies as
are now or may hereafter be placed under the administrative supervision of the Philippines Ambassador to the
United States of America or other officials as the President may designate, shall be known as the Philippine
Mission to the United Nations.
2. The Representative of the Philippines at the seat of the United Nations shall be the Chief of Mission and
shall coordinate at the seat of the United Nations the activities of the Mission in carrying out the instructions
of the President or the Secretary of Foreign Affairs.
3. The Chief of Mission shall be responsible for the administration of the Mission including personnel, budget,
obligation and expenditure of funds which may be made available or allotted by the Secretary of Foreign
Affairs for the conduct, operation and maintenance of its services. The salaries and allowances of the
personnel shall be fixed by the Secretary of Foreign Affairs who shall appoint them in accordance with the
provisions of Executive Order No. 18, dated September 16, 1946, and in pursuance of existing regulations.
The Chief of Mission shall likewise discharge his responsibility in accordance with such rules and regulations
as the Secretary of Foreign Affairs may from time to time prescribe.
